Single-cut baseline and up-enumerated stereo records are compared row for row against a committed mmpdb 3.1.4 oracle, and match for every fixture structure. Not full baseline parity: the fixture deliberately excludes 1,4-disubstituted rings with dependent cis/trans stereo and parent SMILES carrying an invalid stereo tag, both of which diverge at baseline and both of which need an OEMMPA fix before they can be added. mmpdb keys its dedupe on attachment_order.variable_smiles.constant_smiles without the enumeration label, which restores the rows its frag1_indices reference defect would otherwise suppress, so that defect is unobservable at one cut.

Potential-stereocentre detection is exercised through the fixture: centres that survive a cut, a specified tag that is not a real centre and collapses to one achiral form, and prochiral carbons that a cut desymmetrises into new centres. Mixed rather than matched because OEMMPA and mmpdb disagree on two inputs outside the fixture, recorded on the dependent-ring-stereo and invalid-parent-stereo surfaces below.

Open OEMMPA divergence, excluded from the fixture pending a fix. For a ring whose stereocentres are dependent rather than independently chiral (1,4-disubstituted rings such as C[C@H]1CC[C@@H](O)CC1), OEMMPA clears both tags and emits achiral fragments where mmpdb retains the cis/trans relationship, for example OC1CCC([*:1])CC1 against mmpdb O[C@H]1CC[C@@H]([*:1])CC1. This is a baseline-level difference, so it can never be allowlisted. 1,3-disubstituted rings are unaffected and are covered by the fixture. A correct fix needs stereo-aware symmetry refinement; no OEChem predicate distinguishes the two situations.

Open OEMMPA divergence, excluded from the fixture pending a fix. For a parent whose stereo tag is invalid (C[C@H](C)CO, a tag on an atom with two identical methyls), RDKit clears it at parse time so mmpdb emits an achiral baseline plus up-enumerated records, whereas OEMMPA keeps the tag and emits both forms as baseline with no enumerated records. The record content nearly coincides; the enumeration labels do not. Normalising at parse time would change emission cardinality.

Carbon created-stereocentre up-enumeration matches mmpdb for every enumerating fixture structure. OEMMPA additionally enumerates three-coordinate nitrogen with no hydrogens, which mmpdb is_potential_chiral_center excludes, so N,N-dialkylamine and N,N-dialkylsulfonamide motifs are deliberately outside this fixture and remain an open divergence.

Ring-constrained and exocyclic E/Z geometry is verified against the oracle. Acyclic stereogenic double bonds are out of fixture scope: mmpdb asymmetric begin/end bond-direction transfer inverts exactly one of the two cuts flanking such a bond, and RDKit FragmentOnBonds agrees with OEMMPA rather than mmpdb there, so an acyclic case would pin an upstream error.

Explicit design difference. The mmpdb fragment command never produces hydrogen fragmentations; only transform and predict call this surface, and only they emit its `[*][H]` _hydrogen_cut_smiles constant. The committed oracle therefore contains none, and a structural test (a projected fragment with no heavy atom) pins the absence so it cannot become an unnoticed coverage gap.
